text:
After 20 minutes in Dallas, the Jets were down 2-0 and the Stars were doing what they wanted. Arttu Hyry scored at 4:19, Roope Hintz added a backhand late in the period, and nothing in the first suggested a blowout. Then Winnipeg scored five times in the second period and turned a road game into its fifth straight win.

Dylan Samberg started it 71 seconds into the second. Mark Scheifele tied it at 7:03. David Perron put Dallas back in front at 11:14, which our win-probability model had as a 52% to 72% swing for the Stars, and it lasted less than three minutes. Dawson Mercer tied it at 13:55, Scheifele scored on the power play at 18:12 (the goal that moved Winnipeg from 50% to 73%), and Mercer added another with nine seconds left in the period. The Jets won the second 1.96 to 0.73 in expected goals, the quality of their chances, and it was the only period that wasn't close.

Mercer is having a week. He scored twice against his old team, the Devils, in the last game, and scored twice again here. Scheifele finished with two goals and an assist, Kyle Connor and Gabriel Vilardi had a goal and two assists each, and Cole Perfetti set up both Mercer goals. Kyle Connor's goal one minute into the third made it 6-3, and Vilardi and Cole Koepke scored 14 seconds apart late.

The final score flatters the gap. Over the full game Winnipeg had 4.17 expected goals to Dallas's 3.81, Dallas had more shot attempts (65 to 54), and our replays of every shot give the Jets this one 55% of the time. What broke it was goaltending: Jake Oettinger allowed six goals on 27 shots, about 2.7 more than those shots deserved, and Casey DeSmith allowed two on three. Stuart Skinner made 30 saves on the other side, 0.81 goals better than expected.

Dallas is still without Miro Heiskanen, who missed this one, and this was a night when the Stars had the chances but not the saves. Winnipeg is rolling. Five straight wins, and the line of Scheifele, Connor and Vilardi was on the ice for about two expected goals for and under one against.
headline: Jets turn a two-goal hole into an 8-3 rout
